But what is in the choice of the doer, wherever it may come or be done, is clearly not attributed to others.

But so that also through deeds, which those people have lived, and through myths among them, gathering proofs to expose them as foolish, we show more clearly to the listeners that their doctrine is not filled with ignorance, and that not using one's own counsel in actions, nor walking with autonomous judgment, is a charge of utmost folly, as I will recall, having already said it. The stories among them mention Tantalus, Tityus, and Ixion, and the troubles of Sisyphus, and they claim that these people pay the penalties, and rightly so, for the things they willed. For Tantalus, they say he is punished, with a stone suspended over his head, and always expecting dangers. If one were to ask the reason for his suffering, they would say it is because he had an uncontrolled tongue and a most shameful disease. Tityus, they say, is stretched out over nine whole acres, and vultures tear at his liver, and they claim that this is a proof of his uncontrolled lust. Ixion and Sisyphus, the one is punished, they say, with wheels and circular motions, and the other with long toil, and they assign various faults to these people to make their punishments seem just.

But, as they truly think, according to their conversation and intention, we consider man to be subject to the necessities of fate, not to the things they have wrongly named, but to the fate that calls to these things, and because each person's judgment is under their own control, having been placed in their hand. Or, on the one hand, they should be unaware of the unbearable punishments and the immortal torments, and the generation that has acquired more should be blamed and subject to the punishers, if there are any who have decided to do this. Or, if someone says that they are justly punished, let necessity be introduced to us, and let the excess from fate be removed, so that the crimes of Tantalus and Sisyphus may be seen. For if the law of the just is known to us, that not the sinners, but others, are punished in their place, how will it not be clear that nothing could be more wretched than the gods they have established, if those who have been entrusted to judge and distribute all things do not have the power to judge correctly? How are not those among us who bring forth a straight judgment on each person better, having recognized what is fitting for the just to receive? They consider that those who are guilty of shameful things should be hated, and they censure those who have been convicted of transgressing, proportionally to their errors. But these things seem to pertain to your poets and orators. Listen to what our wise men say.

A man's foolishness corrupts his way, and he blames God in his heart. If someone were free from foolishness, he would not have a corrupted way, nor would he blame God's nature. For those who have established their own mind as a guide and teacher, and as a noble judge, always strive to do the best. However, they exchange the best counsel and action with a certain tone. Therefore, it is not fate or birth that makes a person a worker of evil or a lover of good, but rather all people walk voluntarily in both directions. And wherever each person thinks, they necessarily direct their own affairs without anything hindering them. If it is necessary to add something to what has been said, I will also discuss the ignorance of the Greeks and how their father fell into this lack of counsel. That evil demon, the father of sin, showed man to be a transgressor of God's command. He, like a tyrant, dominated us through deception, and he feared the free nature that was in man.

But lest using his own autonomy he destroy the pleasure that tyrannizes the one drawing to freedom; rather lamenting the sins, having spoken, he rises to the advantages from the beginning and dwelling on the works of righteousness, he is already found unworthy of the help from above; he devised another method of deception, which, having always made this the weapon of his own malice, stealing as it were the greater part of the grief over the sins, always fighting through cunning the reproofs from his conscience, saying 'You yourselves are not responsible for not being able to do better'; and 'God has not placed sobriety in your power'; 'A necessary yoke has been laid upon you'; 'Fate and birth control and it is necessary to do what seems to them'; 'The evil one handles man with such deceptions and having stolen him away from the doctrines of truth, makes him more prepared for every sin'; 'For fate, placing the escape in the things according to himself, and saying that he is subject to the unbreakable bonds of birth, will not submit to any punishment for which he may seem to be guilty'; 'But in these things, they, having despised sobriety'; 'Let the heralds of the Church, those who have put on Christ and bear the mind of truth, say'; 'For we do not ignore his thoughts'; 'So that those thus sick with foolishness, guilty of the recently spoken deceptions, and setting their own thought against the will of the lawgiver, may not have war against the one they least ought, let them hear what we said from the beginning…

Let us make peace with him, let us end the enmity. Let war and battle cease, let us give our right hands to the Savior. Let us ask for peace through faith. pass_b_english: Those who fulfill the debt of nature, which is their natural obligation, destroy their own autonomy, because they do not believe they have control over their own choices, nor do they wish to be masters of their own will.

Instead, they attribute the blame for their actions to the votes of others, rather than taking responsibility themselves, and they claim that fate and birth balance the life of each individual, assigning the best things to some and opposing others.

This idea is similar to setting up a charioteer, only to entrust the charioteering to another, which means the charioteer would not be responsible for winning or losing, nor would they be accountable for any suffering that may occur.
The true responsibility lies with those who have control over the chariot, not with the one standing on it, and ultimately, the choice of the doer is what matters, and it is not attributed to others.

To further expose the foolishness of these people, we will examine their deeds and the myths that have been passed down among them, and by doing so, we will gather evidence to demonstrate that their doctrine is not rooted in ignorance, but rather in a lack of self-control and a failure to use their own judgment in their actions.

The stories of Tantalus, Tityus, and Ixion, as well as the troubles of Sisyphus, are often cited as examples of people who have been justly punished for their wrongdoing, with Tantalus being punished for his uncontrolled tongue and his shameful disease, Tityus being stretched out over nine acres and having his liver torn at by vultures as a proof of his uncontrolled lust, Ixion being punished with wheels and circular motions, and Sisyphus being forced to toil for a long time.

These punishments are seen as just and fitting for the crimes that these individuals have committed, but according to their own understanding, humans are subject to the necessities of fate, rather than being responsible for the things they have done wrong, and if the law of the just is known to us, that not the sinners, but others, are punished in their place, it will not be clear that nothing could be more wretched than the gods they have established, if those who have been entrusted to judge and distribute all things do not have the power to judge correctly.

For if it is known that the law of the just is such that not the sinners, but others, are punished in their place, it will be clear that nothing could be more wretched than the gods they have established, and it will be obvious to everyone that this is the case.
A man's foolishness corrupts his way, and he blames God in his heart (Proverbs 19:3).

If someone were truly free from foolishness, they would not have a corrupted path, nor would they blame God's nature, for those who have established their own mind as a guide and teacher, and as a noble judge, always strive to do the best, and they exchange the best counsel and action with a certain tone.

Human beings have the capacity to choose their own path in life, and they walk voluntarily in both directions, towards good or evil, and it is not fate or birth that determines a person's actions, but rather their own free will.

The evil demon, who is the father of sin, has deceived humanity and led them astray from God's command through deception, and he has dominated us and feared the free nature that is inherent in humanity, trying to convince us that we are not capable of doing better, that God has not given us the power to be sober-minded, and that a necessary yoke has been laid upon us, saying 'You yourselves are not responsible for not being able to do better; God has not placed sobriety in your power; a necessary yoke has been laid upon you; fate and birth control and it is necessary to do what seems to them'.

But this is a deception designed to lead us away from the truth and into the depths of sin, and the evil demon handles man with such deceptions, having stolen him away from the doctrines of truth, and makes him more prepared for every sin, for fate, placing the escape in the things according to himself, and saying that he is subject to the unbreakable bonds of birth, will not submit to any punishment for which he may seem to be guilty.

Let us heed the words of the heralds of the Church, who have put on Christ and bear the mind of truth, and let us strive for peace, and end the enmity that divides us, and let war and battle cease, and instead offer our right hands to the Savior, and through faith, we can ask for peace and say with the prophet, 'Lord, our God, give us peace; Lord, possess us, we know no other besides you, we call upon your name' (Isaiah 26:12-13).

This message will be beneficial for the Greek children and those who have recently entered the Church, and for those who are armed with the weapons of ignorance, trained as unwise soldiers, and are fighting against the truth.
